subject: Control plane savings architecture & quantization recommendations
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@novum.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Control plane savings architecture & quantization recommendations

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to capture a concise starting point for how we can structure a pilot to surface savings from batching/KV-cache and quantization without affecting your latency targets. High level proposal below, details attached (controlplane-savings-v1.pdf + quant-recs.xlsx):

- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, 2 production-like routes (inference + reranking).
- Credit structure: 8,000 USD in onboarding credits + commit to a 3-month reserved slab for predictable throughput. We typically split pilot credits 60/40 (runtime credits / advisory & tuning credits).
- Technical knobs:
  - Batch window: 10–30ms target for 95th latency; adaptive batching during peaks up to 80ms for throughput runs.
  - KV cache: recommend prefix/KV caching for 70% of requests (expected hit-rate 0.65–0.8 in your traffic profile) — reduces token compute by ~20–28%.
  - Quantization: two-path approach — PTQ int8 for non-safety-critical routes, and 4-bit (QLoRA-style) evaluation on a small subset to validate quality retention before wider rollout.
- Expected first-order token cost delta: 25–34% reduction vs baseline FP16 when combining caching + int8 batching.

Ask for Novum team: can you share the latency SLO per route (p95) and a representative sample of average sequence length? That will let us size the slab and model variant we allocate for the pilot.

Attached: controlplane-savings-v1.pdf (proposal), quant-recs.xlsx (recommendations matrix).

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min follow-up this week to walk through numbers.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Karthik —

Appreciate the write-up and attachments. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we lock in the pilot:

1) Pilot credits: is the 8k one-time credit intended to cover both test traffic and the quantization evaluation/benchmarks? Our procurement team will need a line-item description.
2) Latency SLO: our internal SLO for the main inference route is p95 <= 120ms (end-to-end), and average sequence length is ~220 tokens.
3) Quality guardrails: for the 4-bit path, do you have in-house evaluation metrics we can run? We need to know expected regression thresholds (e.g., <2% drop in top-1 accuracy for rerank).

Procurement (cc): what procurement info do you need from Redwood to get an ND/PO in place for a pilot?

Happy to take a quick screenshare tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,

Olivia — thanks for the fast reply and the SLO/seq length info, that helps. A few concrete notes from engineering on how to operationalize without increasing p95 beyond your 120ms target:

- Credits: the 8k covers both runtime test traffic and the post-run quantization evaluation (we allocate ~15% of credits to the advisory/tuning bucket which covers evaluation jobs). We'll provide a simple line-item statement for Procurement.

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@novum.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Novum.ai Procurement <procurement@novum.ai>
Date: 2028-07-25T14:05:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Control plane savings architecture & quantization recommendations

(continued)

- Latency guardrails: start with an adaptive batching window set to max 30ms for interactive requests. For background rerank batches we can extend windows to 80–100ms where throughput matters more. With your p95=120ms target we expect room to absorb an int8 path for 70–75% of realtime traffic with no degradation.

- Quantization recommendations:
  - Model family: for Llama-style 34B+ we recommend per-channel symmetric int8 (PTQ) as the first pass. That yields ~1.7–2.4x speedups on our inference runtime depending on kernel availability.
  - For more aggressive compression, run a constrained QAT/LLM-ft 4-bit test on 5k validation pairs (we can run this under the advisory credits). Check quality delta: target <1.5% relative drop on your rerank pass metrics, otherwise fallback to int8.

- KV cache sizing: given 220 token average, we propose a 3-shard KV cache with hot-key affinity for the expected 65–80% hit-rate. That design lowers repeated token compute for session-heavy traffic and pairs well with batching to reduce cost by the 20–28% band Karthik outlined.

Attached: pilot-credit-calculator.csv (simple example split + expected token burn by week).

I can run the quant evaluation for you — if you grant us a short-lived eval key we will run the 5k validation and return quality reports and a recommended fallback policy within 7 business days.

— Irene
